bull_bear.body: Strategic divestiture/closure of non-core, loss-making international assets (Awuko, Foskor) to stop cash bleed. Strong FCF generation (56.6% of PAT) supports INR 400cr growth capex without leverage (D/E 0.08). Dividend income from subsidiaries utilized in standalone PAT.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical sanctions on VAW Russia continuing to depress consolidated top-line; Delay in SCOMET approval for defense exports; Execution risk on ramping new semiconductor/SOFC capacities; Raw material price volatility (Zircon sand, energy).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Decisive and pragmatic on cutting losses (Awuko/Foskor closure); Confident on standalone operational turnaround and H2 momentum; Long-term optimistic on 'Aspiration 2030' transformational pillars but conservative on near-term consolidated guidance due to base effects.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'doubling' of Q4 standalone PAT masks a one-off INR 76cr dividend inflow; however, the operational PBIT growth (+23% standalone) confirms genuine volume recovery. The exit of Awuko/Foskor removes a ~INR 343cr revenue drag but eliminates ~INR 100cr+ annual loss, effectively resetting the consolidated margin baseline from ~4% to ~8-9% immediately.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Largest producer of Fused Alumina in India; among the largest global producers of Silicon Carbide grains; leading market player in Abrasives; second-largest global producer of Metallised Cylinders; and a leader in thermal and corrosion protection for critical applications.
- Integrated materials-science value chain — raw-material sourcing, design & engineering (application engineering, simulation, thermal/corrosion audits) through to manufacturing and distribution — across manufacturing facilities in seven countries with customers in 60+ countries.
- Distribution network built as a competitive moat in Abrasives, reinforced by dealer-led growth programmes, sub-dealer activation and digital enablement of secondary sales.
- High barriers to entry in Metallized Cylinders (vacuum interrupters) driven by installed capacity, stringent OEM qualification requirements and high OEM lock-in.
- Strong new-product vitality — new products contributed approximately 16.5% of total Abrasives revenue in FY 2025-26.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Overseas subsidiary / geopolitical exposure — Russian subsidiary Volzhsky Abrasive Works remains on the US Treasury OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, restricting its addressable markets largely to Russia/CIS; Rhodius Abrasives (Germany) saw margin depletion from a one-time operational transition and price pressure; CUMI Awuko (Germany) continued to underperform on revenue and profitability; and Foskor Zirconia (South Africa) was hit by commodity price movements, exchange-rate fluctuations and rising input costs, with management determining it can no longer continue operations viably.
- Customer concentration — High dependency on a few large customers creates concentration risk; loss of one or more key customers could lead to a substantial drop in revenues, prompting the Company to pursue derisking via new/emerging applications and reduced dependency on one or two segments/customers.
- Raw-material price volatility and supply — Key inputs — Bauxite, Alumina, Calcined Alumina, Zirconia sand, Quartz and Graphite — carry high price volatility; severe price discrimination by overseas players is impacting the business, with geo-political shifts also affecting sources of supply and plant capacity utilisation.
- Import-led pricing pressure and trade policy — Pricing pressure from low-cost imports and price discrimination by international players affects competitiveness; high import tariffs, particularly from the US, pose a risk to exports and external demand.
- Foreign exchange risk — The Company deals in multiple currencies and is exposed to exchange-rate risk on imports and exports, mitigated through a country-based forex policy, monitoring and hedging instruments, and efforts toward natural hedging.
- Energy and fuel cost exposure — Power requirements (largely driven by the Electrominerals business) are sourced from State Electricity Boards, open-access arrangements and own solar generation; fuel costs tied to high-temperature Abrasives/Ceramics processes directly affect profitability, and the tenure extension for the Kerala hydroelectric project remains pending.
- Cybersecurity — The Company is implementing a risk-based cybersecurity framework (aligned with NIST and ISO 27001) across IT and OT systems; implementation is still in progress and being extended to global entities in a phased manner, with cybersecurity insurance in place to offset financial risk.
- Macro and geopolitical headwinds — Higher energy costs and raw-material inflation from the Middle East conflict, a potential monsoon deficit affecting the rural economy, heightened global geopolitical tensions, slowing external demand and a possible Chinese economic slowdown are flagged as risks to the business outlook.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: CUMI is a globally integrated materials-science company operating through three core businesses — Abrasives, Ceramics (Industrial Ceramics and Super Refractories) and Electrominerals — covering the value chain from raw-material sourcing and integrated manufacturing to marketing and distribution. It serves industrial, retail and OEM customers across automotive, engineering, infrastructure, steel, mining, power, aerospace & defence, semiconductors, electronics and other sectors through manufacturing facilities in seven countries and sales in over 60 countries.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Abrasives:** Bonded Abrasives, Coated Abrasives, Super Abrasives, Metal Working Fluids, Thin Wheels
- **Electrominerals:** Fused Alumina, Silicon Carbide grains, High-purity Silicon Carbide (5N/6N Hp-SiC)
- **Industrial Ceramics:** Wear Ceramics, Precision Engineered Ceramics (Solid Oxide Fuel Cell / electrolyser components), Metallized Cylinders (vacuum interrupters), AMB/DBC substrates for power electronics, Semiconductor wafer-fabrication ceramic components, Aerospace & Defence armour ceramics
- **Refractories / Anti-corrosion:** Refractories, Anti-corrosive solutions, Advanced Composites

Defense ballistic ceramics scaling post-SCOMET approval. Treated grains target 20% mix by 2030.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Disciplined capital allocation and portfolio optimisation, including strategic review of select overseas businesses.
- Shift in Electrominerals toward specialised, high-purity, value-added materials away from commoditised products.
- Industrial Ceramics roadmap to become a leading global player in advanced ceramics, strengthening core segments (Wear Ceramics, Metallized Cylinders, Precision Engineered Ceramics) while building presence in Semiconductors, Electronics, Aerospace and Defence.
- Objective of becoming a leader in metallized alumina cylinders for vacuum interrupters, via continued capability and capacity expansion.
- Abrasives: strengthen distribution network as a competitive moat, deepen customer engagement, and build execution excellence via sharper market segmentation and structured go-to-market models.
- Refractories/Composites: strengthen corrosion protection and advanced composites capabilities through the Integrated Manufacturing Excellence (IMEx) programme, process improvement and automation.
- Capability-first, partnership-led development and phased customer-led market entry in high-growth emerging segments (Semiconductors, Electronics, Aerospace & Defence).
- Continued investment in capacity expansion, technology upgradation, digitalisation and sustainability initiatives to sustain export competitiveness.
- The Company follows a disciplined capital-allocation approach guided by its historical dividend payout ratio, operating performance and long-term growth/investment plans. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a final dividend of Rs.2.50 per equity share (in addition to an interim dividend of Rs.1.50 per equity share already paid). The Company maintained a net debt-free standalone position and generated healthy free cash flow, reinvesting in strategic growth platforms (its highest-ever capex programme in the year) while also undertaking portfolio optimisation, including the voluntary winding-up of an underperforming German subsidiary and a strategic review of a non-viable South African subsidiary.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 was the Company's highest-ever capital expenditure year (consolidated capex of Rs.3,094 million, standalone Rs.2,352 million per the Chairman's letter), directed at Thin Wheels production in Abrasives, ceramics for Semiconductor Equipment & Aerospace/Defence applications in Industrial Ceramics, Fused Alumina capacity expansion, and materials for Solid Oxide Fuel Cells in Electrominerals. The Abrasives business commissioned a Greenfield Thin Wheels manufacturing facility at Hosur using production lines/technology acquired from DRONCO GmbH, Germany, in March 2026, positioned as the Centre of Excellence for thin wheels. The Electrominerals (EMD) business has set multi-year expansion plans: capacity addition in fused alumina (primarily treated products), expansion of the Zirconia portfolio through furnacing and grain-processing capability additions, and a Thermal Spray portfolio revamp with an exclusive integrated furnacing line and an automated grain-processing facility; capacity expansion for HpSiC 5N-purity and advanced nitrides manufacturing has progressed significantly and is expected to complete in FY 2026-27, and new treated-grain facilities (Zirconia and Treated Alumina) are scheduled to commence commercial production over FY 2026-27 to ease existing capacity constraints. Under the IMEx (Integrated Manufacturing Excellence) programme, Electrominerals also initiated furnace-capacity expansion, treated-alumina facilities (rotary and tunnel routes) and a 110kV substation upgrade, all underway during the year; Industrial Ceramics invested in precision capability across Semiconductor, Defence, Electronics and Automotive applications; and Super Refractories added automation (batching, tamping, Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems) and upgraded composite-processing capabilities. Per BRSR Principle 2 disclosures, capex directed to technologies improving environmental/social impact was 10.0% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (versus 24.9% in FY 2024-25), funding a Solar Group captive power plant, sewage-treatment facility upgradation with a new sludge dewatering screw press, kiln refractory improvements for waste-heat recovery, and an air-cooled inverter chiller system.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Automotive sector expected to normalise in FY 2026-27.
- Demand from construction and infrastructure sectors likely to remain strong, supported by public sector capex and consumer demand.
- Expanding railway infrastructure, strengthening indigenous defence manufacturing and accelerating adoption of high-precision, automated production expected to drive demand for high-performance abrasives.
- Recent Free Trade Agreement (FTA) signed by the Indian Government strengthens opportunities in export-oriented manufacturing, though ongoing U.S. tariff-policy uncertainty remains a key risk to export competitiveness and demand visibility.
- Demand for locally manufactured abrasives expected to strengthen due to import-related supply uncertainties following West Asia conflict disruption.
- Power Transmission & Distribution demand drivers expected to remain favourable, supported by grid modernisation and the phased replacement of SF6-based equipment.
- SOFC ecosystem witnessing accelerated adoption, driven by rising power requirements from AI data centres and the broader energy transition.
- Electronics applications expected to expand on rising adoption of EV power modules and growing demand from Healthcare, Aerospace and Defence.
- Semiconductor value chain poised for growth on advanced-packaging requirements and AI-led fab investments, with conversion contingent on product-qualification milestones and customer programme timelines.
- Competitive intensity expected to remain elevated across select verticals, particularly wear applications, from low-cost imports and regional fabricators.
- Refractories/Composites outlook remains positive, supported by investment in industrial infrastructure, energy systems, chemicals, glass and defence process industries.
- Corrosion protection business (within Super Refractories) emerged as a key growth driver, supported by a robust order pipeline and strong project execution.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: CUMI delivered a strong Q4 rebound with standalone PAT doubling YoY, driven by volume recovery and export growth in Electrominerals, while proactively initiating closure of loss-making European and South African subsidiaries (Awuko, Foskor) to clean up the consolidated P&L. The strategic pivot towards high-margin transformational products (semiconductor components, defense ceramics, SOFC) positions the company for a structural re-rating despite near-term consolidated headwinds from sanctioned Russian assets.

open.item: Standalone Abrasives expected to grow about 12% in FY27 (versus 6.2% in FY26).
RHODIUS FY27 sales expected to grow about 5% with FY27 PAT expected to be a very small loss (versus EUR 2.6 million loss in FY26).
Achieved 5N purity on HPSiC and will work on securing customers over FY27; 6N purity technology route initiated with a pilot-scale facility.
FY27 capex expected at about INR 400 crores across capacity/capability projects (advanced ceramics, brown-fused alumina, thermal spray powders, zirconia, refractory tunnel kiln, 110kV substation).
Consolidated Electrominerals FY27 margin expected at 9-9.5% (FY26 reported 5.6%; 9.1% excluding Foskor loss).
Consolidated Ceramics FY27 margin expected at 20.5-21% (FY26 reported 20.2%).
Consolidated Abrasives FY27 margin expected around 9.5-10% (FY26 reported 4.3%; 7.9% excluding Awuko losses).
Consolidated Electrominerals FY27 sales expected to decline 6.5-7% due to Foskor Zirconia closure; excluding Foskor (INR 235 crores FY26), growth would be 8-9%.
Consolidated Ceramics FY27 growth expected in the range of 15-15.5% (management also cited about 14% for the segment).
Consolidated Abrasives FY27 sales expected to grow 5.5-6%; excluding Awuko (INR 108 crores FY26), growth would be 11-12%.
FY27 consolidated sales expected to grow approximately 4-4.5%; excluding Foskor Zirconia and Awuko (INR 343 crores of FY26 sales), comparable growth would be 11-12%.
Metallized cylinder capacity expansion to happen in a phased manner over the next 18-24 months (three phases).

Semiconductor wafer-fab-equipment components facility (INR 66 crore first module) to commence serial supplies in FY27 with gradual line utilisation ramp-up; material revenue expected from 2029 onwards.
FY2030 ESG targets: increase renewable energy use to 50%, reduce emission intensity by 25% and lower energy intensity by 20% from FY2025 levels.
Aspiration 2030: specialty products (zirconia-based) share to increase from 8% currently to 18-20% by 2030; transformational products to contribute around 10% by 2030.
Aspiration 2030: treated-grain share to increase from 5-6% currently to nearly 20% by 2030.
Aspiration 2030: Electrominerals core products (BFA/WFA/SiC) share to fall from 85% currently to 55-60% by 2030 as other categories scale.

Aerospace & defence ballistic ceramics facility (INR 49 crore) commissioned with STANAG 4 and BIS Threat Level 5/6 qualifications; awaiting SCOMET approval; business expected to scale up gradually around 2030.
Long-term (5-year) aspiration to grow the company by 2 times with sustained profitability.
Plan to increase R&D spend 4 to 5 times over the next 5 to 6 years to fuel innovation.

currentContext.strengths: Largest producer of Fused Alumina in India; among the largest global producers of Silicon Carbide grains; leading market player in Abrasives; second-largest global producer of Metallised Cylinders; and a leader in thermal and corrosion protection for critical applications.|Integrated materials-science value chain — raw-material sourcing, design & engineering (application engineering, simulation, thermal/corrosion audits) through to manufacturing and distribution — across manufacturing facilities in seven countries with customers in 60+ countries.|Distribution network built as a competitive moat in Abrasives, reinforced by dealer-led growth programmes, sub-dealer activation and digital enablement of secondary sales.|High barriers to entry in Metallized Cylinders (vacuum interrupters) driven by installed capacity, stringent OEM qualification requirements and high OEM lock-in.|Strong new-product vitality — new products contributed approximately 16.5% of total Abrasives revenue in FY 2025-26.
currentContext.strategies: Disciplined capital allocation and portfolio optimisation, including strategic review of select overseas businesses.|Shift in Electrominerals toward specialised, high-purity, value-added materials away from commoditised products.|Industrial Ceramics roadmap to become a leading global player in advanced ceramics, strengthening core segments (Wear Ceramics, Metallized Cylinders, Precision Engineered Ceramics) while building presence in Semiconductors, Electronics, Aerospace and Defence.|Objective of becoming a leader in metallized alumina cylinders for vacuum interrupters, via continued capability and capacity expansion.|Abrasives: strengthen distribution network as a competitive moat, deepen customer engagement, and build execution excellence via sharper market segmentation and structured go-to-market models.|Refractories/Composites: strengthen corrosion protection and advanced composites capabilities through the Integrated Manufacturing Excellence (IMEx) programme, process improvement and automation.|Capability-first, partnership-led development and phased customer-led market entry in high-growth emerging segments (Semiconductors, Electronics, Aerospace & Defence).|Continued investment in capacity expansion, technology upgradation, digitalisation and sustainability initiatives to sustain export competitiveness.|The Company follows a disciplined capital-allocation approach guided by its historical dividend payout ratio, operating performance and long-term growth/investment plans. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a final dividend of Rs.2.50 per equity share (in addition to an interim dividend of Rs.1.50 per equity share already paid). The Company maintained a net debt-free standalone position and generated healthy free cash flow, reinvesting in strategic growth platforms (its highest-ever capex programme in the year) while also undertaking portfolio optimisation, including the voluntary winding-up of an underperforming German subsidiary and a strategic review of a non-viable South African subsidiary.
currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was the Company's highest-ever capital expenditure year (consolidated capex of Rs.3,094 million, standalone Rs.2,352 million per the Chairman's letter), directed at Thin Wheels production in Abrasives, ceramics for Semiconductor Equipment & Aerospace/Defence applications in Industrial Ceramics, Fused Alumina capacity expansion, and materials for Solid Oxide Fuel Cells in Electrominerals. The Abrasives business commissioned a Greenfield Thin Wheels manufacturing facility at Hosur using production lines/technology acquired from DRONCO GmbH, Germany, in March 2026, positioned as the Centre of Excellence for thin wheels. The Electrominerals (EMD) business has set multi-year expansion plans: capacity addition in fused alumina (primarily treated products), expansion of the Zirconia portfolio through furnacing and grain-processing capability additions, and a Thermal Spray portfolio revamp with an exclusive integrated furnacing line and an automated grain-processing facility; capacity expansion for HpSiC 5N-purity and advanced nitrides manufacturing has progressed significantly and is expected to complete in FY 2026-27, and new treated-grain facilities (Zirconia and Treated Alumina) are scheduled to commence commercial production over FY 2026-27 to ease existing capacity constraints. Under the IMEx (Integrated Manufacturing Excellence) programme, Electrominerals also initiated furnace-capacity expansion, treated-alumina facilities (rotary and tunnel routes) and a 110kV substation upgrade, all underway during the year; Industrial Ceramics invested in precision capability across Semiconductor, Defence, Electronics and Automotive applications; and Super Refractories added automation (batching, tamping, Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems) and upgraded composite-processing capabilities. Per BRSR Principle 2 disclosures, capex directed to technologies improving environmental/social impact was 10.0% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (versus 24.9% in FY 2024-25), funding a Solar Group captive power plant, sewage-treatment facility upgradation with a new sludge dewatering screw press, kiln refractory improvements for waste-heat recovery, and an air-cooled inverter chiller system.

risks.note: Russian subsidiary Volzhsky Abrasive Works remains on the US Treasury OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, restricting its addressable markets largely to Russia/CIS; Rhodius Abrasives (Germany) saw margin depletion from a one-time operational transition and price pressure; CUMI Awuko (Germany) continued to underperform on revenue and profitability; and Foskor Zirconia (South Africa) was hit by commodity price movements, exchange-rate fluctuations and rising input costs, with management determining it can no longer continue operations viably.

High dependency on a few large customers creates concentration risk; loss of one or more key customers could lead to a substantial drop in revenues, prompting the Company to pursue derisking via new/emerging applications and reduced dependency on one or two segments/customers.

Key inputs — Bauxite, Alumina, Calcined Alumina, Zirconia sand, Quartz and Graphite — carry high price volatility; severe price discrimination by overseas players is impacting the business, with geo-political shifts also affecting sources of supply and plant capacity utilisation.

risks.risk: Import-led pricing pressure and trade policy
risks.note: Pricing pressure from low-cost imports and price discrimination by international players affects competitiveness; high import tariffs, particularly from the US, pose a risk to exports and external demand.

The Company deals in multiple currencies and is exposed to exchange-rate risk on imports and exports, mitigated through a country-based forex policy, monitoring and hedging instruments, and efforts toward natural hedging.

Power requirements (largely driven by the Electrominerals business) are sourced from State Electricity Boards, open-access arrangements and own solar generation; fuel costs tied to high-temperature Abrasives/Ceramics processes directly affect profitability, and the tenure extension for the Kerala hydroelectric project remains pending.

The Company is implementing a risk-based cybersecurity framework (aligned with NIST and ISO 27001) across IT and OT systems; implementation is still in progress and being extended to global entities in a phased manner, with cybersecurity insurance in place to offset financial risk.

Higher energy costs and raw-material inflation from the Middle East conflict, a potential monsoon deficit affecting the rural economy, heightened global geopolitical tensions, slowing external demand and a possible Chinese economic slowdown are flagged as risks to the business outlook.

one-line thesis: CUMI delivered a strong Q4 rebound with standalone PAT doubling YoY, driven by volume recovery and export growth in Electrominerals, while proactively initiating closure of loss-making European and South African subsidiaries (Awuko, Foskor) to clean up the consolidated P&L. The strategic pivot towards high-margin transformational products (semiconductor components, defense ceramics, SOFC) positions the company for a structural re-rating despite near-term consolidated headwinds from sanctioned Russian assets.

FY27 Guidance: INR 400cr focused on power electronics substrates, thermal spray powders, and Refractories tunnel kiln.
capital allocation: Strategic divestiture/closure of non-core, loss-making international assets (Awuko, Foskor) to stop cash bleed. Strong FCF generation (56.6% of PAT) supports INR 400cr growth capex without leverage (D/E 0.08). Dividend income from subsidiaries utilized in standalone PAT.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical sanctions on VAW Russia continuing to depress consolidated top-line; Delay in SCOMET approval for defense exports; Execution risk on ramping new semiconductor/SOFC capacities; Raw material price volatility (Zircon sand, energy).
management quality / tone: Decisive and pragmatic on cutting losses (Awuko/Foskor closure); Confident on standalone operational turnaround and H2 momentum; Long-term optimistic on 'Aspiration 2030' transformational pillars but conservative on near-term consolidated guidance due to base effects.
non-obvious takeaways: The 'doubling' of Q4 standalone PAT masks a one-off INR 76cr dividend inflow; however, the operational PBIT growth (+23% standalone) confirms genuine volume recovery. The exit of Awuko/Foskor removes a ~INR 343cr revenue drag but eliminates ~INR 100cr+ annual loss, effectively resetting the consolidated margin baseline from ~4% to ~8-9% immediately.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Automotive sector expected to normalise in FY 2026-27.
- Demand from construction and infrastructure sectors likely to remain strong, supported by public sector capex and consumer demand.
- Expanding railway infrastructure, strengthening indigenous defence manufacturing and accelerating adoption of high-precision, automated production expected to drive demand for high-performance abrasives.
- Recent Free Trade Agreement (FTA) signed by the Indian Government strengthens opportunities in export-oriented manufacturing, though ongoing U.S. tariff-policy uncertainty remains a key risk to export competitiveness and demand visibility.
- Demand for locally manufactured abrasives expected to strengthen due to import-related supply uncertainties following West Asia conflict disruption.
- Power Transmission & Distribution demand drivers expected to remain favourable, supported by grid modernisation and the phased replacement of SF6-based equipment.
- SOFC ecosystem witnessing accelerated adoption, driven by rising power requirements from AI data centres and the broader energy transition.
- Electronics applications expected to expand on rising adoption of EV power modules and growing demand from Healthcare, Aerospace and Defence.
- Semiconductor value chain poised for growth on advanced-packaging requirements and AI-led fab investments, with conversion contingent on product-qualification milestones and customer programme timelines.
- Competitive intensity expected to remain elevated across select verticals, particularly wear applications, from low-cost imports and regional fabricators.
- Refractories/Composites outlook remains positive, supported by investment in industrial infrastructure, energy systems, chemicals, glass and defence process industries.
- Corrosion protection business (within Super Refractories) emerged as a key growth driver, supported by a robust order pipeline and strong project execution.

The Abrasives business commissioned a Greenfield Thin Wheels manufacturing facility at Hosur using production lines/technology acquired from DRONCO GmbH, Germany, in March 2026, positioned as the Centre of Excellence for thin wheels. The Electrominerals (EMD) business has set multi-year expansion plans: capacity addition in fused alumina (primarily treated products), expansion of the Zirconia portfolio through furnacing and grain-processing capability additions, and a Thermal Spray portfolio revamp with an exclusive integrated furnacing line and an automated grain-processing facility; capacity expansion for HpSiC 5N-purity and advanced nitrides manufacturing has progressed significantly and is expected to complete in FY 2026-27, and new treated-grain facilities (Zirconia and Treated Alumina) are scheduled to commence commercial production over FY 2026-27 to ease existing capacity constraints. Under the IMEx (Integrated Manufacturing Excellence) programme, Electrominerals also initiated furnace-capacity expansion, treated-alumina facilities (rotary and tunnel routes) and a 110kV substation upgrade, all underway during the year; Industrial Ceramics invested in precision capability across Semiconductor, Defence, Electronics and Automotive applications; and Super Refractories added automation (batching, tamping, Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems) and upgraded composite-processing capabilities. Per BRSR Principle 2 disclosures, capex directed to technologies improving environmental/social impact was 10.0% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (versus 24.9% in FY 2024-25), funding a Solar Group captive power plant, sewage-treatment facility upgradation with a new sludge dewatering screw press, kiln refractory improvements for waste-heat recovery, and an air-cooled inverter chiller system.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Decisive and pragmatic on cutting losses (Awuko/Foskor closure); Confident on standalone operational turnaround and H2 momentum; Long-term optimistic on 'Aspiration 2030' transformational pillars but conservative on near-term consolidated guidance due to base effects.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest producer of Fused Alumina in India; among the largest global producers of Silicon Carbide grains; leading market player in Abrasives; second-largest global producer of Metallised Cylinders; and a leader in thermal and corrosion protection for critical applications.
- Integrated materials-science value chain — raw-material sourcing, design & engineering (application engineering, simulation, thermal/corrosion audits) through to manufacturing and distribution — across manufacturing facilities in seven countries with customers in 60+ countries.
- Distribution network built as a competitive moat in Abrasives, reinforced by dealer-led growth programmes, sub-dealer activation and digital enablement of secondary sales.
- High barriers to entry in Metallized Cylinders (vacuum interrupters) driven by installed capacity, stringent OEM qualification requirements and high OEM lock-in.
- Strong new-product vitality — new products contributed approximately 16.5% of total Abrasives revenue in FY 2025-26.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical sanctions on VAW Russia continuing to depress consolidated top-line; Delay in SCOMET approval for defense exports; Execution risk on ramping new semiconductor/SOFC capacities; Raw material price volatility (Zircon sand, energy).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 'doubling' of Q4 standalone PAT masks a one-off INR 76cr dividend inflow; however, the operational PBIT growth (+23% standalone) confirms genuine volume recovery. The exit of Awuko/Foskor removes a ~INR 343cr revenue drag but eliminates ~INR 100cr+ annual loss, effectively resetting the consolidated margin baseline from ~4% to ~8-9% immediately.

one-line thesis: CUMI delivered a strong Q4 rebound with standalone PAT doubling YoY, driven by volume recovery and export growth in Electrominerals, while proactively initiating closure of loss-making European and South African subsidiaries (Awuko, Foskor) to clean up the consolidated P&L. financial scorecard: Revenue: Consolidated INR 5,149cr (+6.5% YoY), Standalone INR 3,024cr (+8.6% YoY). EBITDA/Margin: Consolidated PBIT INR 404cr (-25.3% YoY) due to INR 135cr exceptional items (Awuko/Foskor write-downs) and VAW sanctions; Standalone PBIT INR 525cr (+23.4% YoY). PAT: Consolidated impacted by exceptions; Standalone PAT INR 416cr (+29.4% YoY, includes INR 76cr subsidiary dividend). Order Book: Not explicitly quantified but described as 'strong orders' in Defense and SOFC; Refractories seeing deferred project return. Net Debt: Negligible (D/E 0.08); Strong FCF (56.6% of consolidated PAT). One-offs: INR 135cr exceptional charge (INR 119cr Awuko closure, INR 16cr Foskor asset write-down); VAW Russia sales down 35% due to sanctions.
guidance: FY27 Revenue Growth: Consolidated ~4-4.5% (reported), ~11-12% (organic excluding exiting entities); Abrasives +5.5-6% (reported), +11-12% (organic); Ceramics +15-15.5%; Electrominerals -6.5 to -7% (reported due to Foskor exit), +8-9% (organic). Margins: Abrasives 9.5-10%; Ceramics 20.5-21%; Electrominerals 9-9.5%. Capex: INR 400cr planned for FY27.
order book & pipeline: Qualitative strength noted in Defense (STANAG 4 qualified) and SOFC segments with multi-year visibility (2028-2030); Refractories seeing return of deferred glass sector projects.
segment / subsidiary detail: Abrasives: Standalone +6.2% (strong H2 rebound); Consolidated +5.1% (dragged by Rhodius/Awuko). Electrominerals: Standalone +11.1% (Exports doubled to 33% mix); Consolidated +3.7% (VAW Russia sanction impact). Ceramics: Consolidated +9.3% (Industrial Ceramics +7.8%, Refractories +4.7%); Engineering Ceramics +30% driven by SOFC/Data Center demand.
growth verticals / optionality: Transformational products target 10% revenue share by 2030 (vs negligible today): Semiconductor wafer fab components (serial production FY27), SOFC/SOEC powders, Nitrides, Graphene applications. Defense ballistic ceramics scaling post-SCOMET approval. Treated grains target 20% mix by 2030.
margins & cost dynamics: Standalone Abrasive margin compressed 81bps to 15.3% due to H1 volume lows; Consolidated Abrasive margin 4.3% (distorted by Awuko/Rhodius losses), normalizes to ~7.9% ex-exceptions. Guidance implies significant margin expansion to ~10% as loss-makers exit. Energy cost inflation in South Africa cited as key driver for Foskor unviability.
capex / expansion: FY26 Actual: INR 309cr (Standalone INR 235cr). Key projects: Semiconductor component facility (INR 66cr, commissioned), Defense ballistic ceramics (INR 49cr, commissioned), White Fused Alumina furnace upgrade 2->4.5 MVA (INR 53cr), Thin wheel capacity via DRONCO assets (INR 83cr). FY27 Guidance: INR 400cr focused on power electronics substrates, thermal spray powders, and Refractories tunnel kiln.
capital allocation: Strategic divestiture/closure of non-core, loss-making international assets (Awuko, Foskor) to stop cash bleed. Strong FCF generation (56.6% of PAT) supports INR 400cr growth capex without leverage (D/E 0.08). Dividend income from subsidiaries utilized in standalone PAT.
